title: Putin Says Any Sanctions Threat Against India Would 'Boomerang Immediately' Under Modi
excerpt: At the St Petersburg Economic Forum, the Russian president backed India's strategic autonomy, projected $100 billion bilateral trade, and dismissed American pressure on New Delhi as 'detrimental' to international relations.
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin delivered a full-throated defence of India's strategic independence at the St Petersburg International Economic Forum on Saturday, declaring that any Western attempt to pressure New Delhi with sanctions would "boomerang immediately" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership.

The remarks, made during an interaction with heads of global news agencies including PTI, represent Moscow's most explicit public endorsement of India's balancing act between Western and Russian partnerships — and a pointed message to Washington at a moment when the US-India relationship is navigating its own set of pressures.

## 'Nobody Can Dictate to Us'

Putin was characteristically direct when addressing questions about India's potential purchase of the S-500 air defence system and Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jet — advanced Russian weapons platforms that could trigger US sanctions under the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA).

"India always acts as a sovereign country, and under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, any potential threats of sanctions would boomerang immediately," Putin said. "We have been in close talks with Prime Minister Modi for a long while. All the sanctions have been eliminated, and the relationship between the USA and India is developing successfully, as I understand."

The Russian president was emphatic that Moscow would not be pressured into limiting defence cooperation with New Delhi. "Our cooperation with India is not subject to the political environment. Nobody can dictate to us what to deliver or not deliver to India. We will always stand true to commitments given to our partners, especially partners like India."

## A $100 Billion Trade Target

Putin projected that Russia-India bilateral trade would reach $100 billion in the coming years, a significant escalation from the approximately $65 billion recorded in recent years. The growth has been driven largely by India's increased purchases of discounted Russian crude oil following Western sanctions on Moscow after the Ukraine invasion.

"The US is trying to put pressure on India when it comes to cooperation with Russia on some tracks. But everyone has understood that putting pressure on Narendra Modi — and India, that has the largest population in the world — is detrimental for international relations and for bilateral relations," Putin said.

He dismissed the impact of American diplomatic pressure on the India-Russia relationship: "It doesn't matter where this pressure comes from. We don't see any negative consequences."

## Defence Ties: From BrahMos to Su-57

Putin's remarks touched on the deep historical roots of India-Russia military cooperation, noting that "a significant portion of the armed forces of India is equipped with Russian equipment" — a tradition dating back to the Soviet era.

He specifically highlighted joint research and development projects, including the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile, a collaboration between India's Defence Research and Development Organisation and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya that has become a signature achievement of bilateral defence ties. India has since exported BrahMos to the Philippines, making it one of the few jointly developed weapons systems to find third-country buyers.

The question of whether India might acquire the S-500 — Russia's most advanced air defence system capable of intercepting ballistic missiles and hypersonic targets — and the Su-57, which would give India access to a fifth-generation stealth fighter, remains politically sensitive. India's acquisition of the S-400 system in 2021 drew strong objections from Washington, though the Biden administration ultimately chose not to impose CAATSA sanctions.

## BRICS Over G7

Putin used the forum to highlight the growing economic weight of the BRICS bloc — Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa — plus its expanding membership. He noted that BRICS has now surpassed the G7 in aggregate economic output, and lauded India as a "crucial partner" in the grouping.

"India's contributions to the global IT and software sectors are unmatched," Putin said, projecting optimistic growth for BRICS economies relative to their Western counterparts.

The framing is deliberate. As the Iran war reshapes global energy flows and trade patterns, Russia has positioned itself as a reliable alternative to Western-dominated supply chains — offering India discounted oil, advanced weapons, and diplomatic backing in exchange for New Delhi's refusal to join the sanctions regime against Moscow.

## What NRIs Should Watch

For the Indian diaspora, Putin's remarks carry implications beyond geopolitics. India's strategic autonomy — the ability to buy Russian oil, weapons, and technology without fear of Western punishment — has direct consequences for the Indian economy. Cheaper Russian crude has helped cushion the blow of the Iran-driven oil price spike. Russian defence equipment underpins India's military preparedness at a time of heightened border tensions.

But the balancing act has limits. As the US-India trade deal enters its final stages, with both sides describing it as "99 per cent done," Washington's tolerance for India's Russia engagement will be tested. The CAATSA question over the S-500 and Su-57 could become the sharpest edge of that tension.

Modi's challenge remains unchanged: extract maximum value from both partnerships while avoiding the point where one relationship forces a reckoning with the other. Putin's SPIEF performance suggests Moscow is eager to make that reckoning as costly as possible for Washington to force.
